paragraphs: In Shabbat 82a he disagrees with Rav Chisda and Rav Hamnuna; Shabbat 155b [supplied 155a] has “Rav Chanan of Nehardea taught.” But Kiddushin 81b has Rav Chanan of Nehardea arriving at Rav Kahana’s in Pum Nahara. He saw him sitting and studying with an animal before him. He asked, “Does the master not hold that [seclusion is forbidden] even with an animal?” He answered, “It did not occur to me.” In Niddah 66a, Rav Kahana considered saying a ruling, and Rav Chanan of Nehardea responded, etc. Hyman says it appears that in both places it SHOULD READ Rav Nachman of Nehardea, as in Chullin 95b, since, as he states, Rav Kahana of Pum Nahara was Rav Ashi’s teacher.

notes.text: קנה. is Hyman’s folio 155a, not a verb meaning “acquired.” The checked teaching occurs on 155b. Hyman’s Chanan-to-Nachman correction and the chronology of Rav Kahana remain his argument.
